svg.title: Atlas system design: Save & share an issue
svg.desc: Atlas architecture with the "Save & share an issue" flow playing through it, 14 steps through 5 parts.
svg.text: How Atlas saves an issue it can't read

g.text: A fresh key per issue, made with WebCrypto.
STEP 2 OF 14 · REQUEST · READER'S BROWSER → VERCEL
Page count, how long to keep it, and the key only if 'Keep in My magazines' is on.
STEP 3 OF 14 · REQUEST · VERCEL → EXPRESS API
1–96 pages; an editable copy must keep its key on the account.
STEP 5 OF 14 · REQUEST · EXPRESS API → POSTGRES
Forever is for paid plans only.
STEP 6 OF 14 · REQUEST · EXPRESS API → POSTGRES
Owner, page count, expiry, optional key. No title, no words.
STEP 7 OF 14 · REQUEST · EXPRESS API → ISSUES BUCKET
STEP 8 OF 14 · REPLY · EXPRESS API → READER'S BROWSER
201 · id + one upload slot per file
seal() each page and the manifest
1080×1440 carousel slides; title and dek live inside the sealed manifest.
STEP 10 OF 14 · REQUEST · READER'S BROWSER → ISSUES BUCKET
PUT sealed blobs to signed URLs
Bytes never pass through the API.
STEP 11 OF 14 · REQUEST · READER'S BROWSER → EXPRESS API
STEP 12 OF 14 · CHECK · EXPRESS API → ISSUES BUCKET
Checked against the bucket, not taken on trust.
STEP 13 OF 14 · REQUEST · EXPRESS API → POSTGRES
STEP 14 OF 14 · REPLY · EXPRESS API → READER'S BROWSER
The key sits after the #, which browsers never send to a server.
SAVE & SHARE AN ISSUE · 14 STEPS THROUGH 5 PARTS
Pages are sealed in the browser with a per-issue AES-GCM key and uploaded straight to storage; the key goes in the link after #.
Every hop is read from the code: the dot is the request; faded parts take no part in this flow.
